quoted_clause.quote: The Commission adopted Xcel Energy’s proposed tariff framework for very large customers but strengthened it in several key areas to better implement these statutory requirements.

docket.value: MPUC Docket No. 25-289 (Xcel's petition is captioned E002/M-25-___)

cites.quote: Full record information is available in Docket 25-289.

Please take notice that on July 16, 2025, Northern States Power Company doing business as Xcel Energy filed with the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission a Petition requesting approval of its proposed tariffs for Large General Time of Day Service and Large Peak Controlled Time of Day Service customers, including data centers.
Minnesota Public Utilities Commission sent this bulletin at 05/18/2026 01:00 PM CDT

cites.section: NSP-Minnesota Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, Large Load/Data Center Tariff
cites.quote: The tariff, which was approved by the MPUC in June 2026, is mandatory for new loads over 100 MW and includes an incremental cost test, minimum initial term of 15 years, minimum bill provisions, termination and exit fees, and credit requirements.

threshold_mw.value: New loads of 100 MW or more; also new customers of at least 20 MW but less than 100 MW that are system intensive (needing significant system modifications, design, engineering or other expenditures before service)

cites.section: Key approvals, Defining very large customers
cites.quote: The Commission defined “very large customers” for purposes of Xcel’s tariffs as new loads sized 100 megawatts (MW) or greater.

cites.section: Key approvals, Defining very large customers
cites.quote: this new customer class will include any new customer with at least 20 MW but less than 100 MW of load if the customer is “system intensive” ... meaning the customer will require significant system modifications, design, engineering, or other expenditures prior to starting service.

min_demand.value: Minimum bill on 80 percent of the customer's contracted capacity (the Commission raised it from the 75 percent Xcel proposed); in Xcel's proposed sheet the floor applies to the Load Ramp Capacity during the ramp and to the Contract Capacity after it

cites.section: Key approvals, A balanced contract structure
cites.quote: the Commission increased the minimum bill and exit fee proposed by Xcel to 80% of the customer’s contracted capacity to strengthen ratepayer protections.

cites.section: Proposed Sheet No. 32.4, Determination of On Peak Period Demand (redline)
cites.quote: In no month shall the on peak period demand to be billed be less than the current month's Adjusted On Peak Demand in kW, or 75% of the Load Ramp Capacity or Contract Capacity as defined for that time period in the ESA.

contract_term.value: 15-year default contract term (approved); in Xcel's proposed sheet the initial ESA term is at least 15 years including a Load Ramp Period of up to 5 years; 24 months' exit notice (approved)

cites.section: Key approvals, A balanced contract structure
cites.quote: The Commission approved Xcel’s proposed 15-year default contract term and 24 month exit notice period.
Customers subject to this tariff must enter into an ESA with an initial term of at least fifteen (15) years, inclusive of any Load Ramp Period of up to a maximum of five (5) years.

collateral.value: Transmission and distribution upgrades paid by the customer as contributions in aid of construction (Commission). Xcel's proposed sheet requires sufficient credit support in the ESA; its form ESA asks for a guaranty from a US guarantor with no credit rating but a cash balance over 3 billion dollars, or a rating of BBB- (S&P) or Baa3 (Moody's) or better, and on a Credit Event a cash deposit, letter of credit, surety bond or other support for the Company's credit exposure within 30 days, capped at the Guaranty Cap

cites.section: Key approvals, Requiring customer-funded system upgrades
cites.quote: All transmission and distribution upgrades needed to serve very large customers must be paid directly by those customers through Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC).
At a minimum, the following security and risk mitigation requirements will be included in the ESA. a. Sufficient credit support;

cites.section: Attachment G, Retail Customer Form ESA, section 14
cites.quote: either has (i) no Credit Rating but whose Cash Balance is more than three billion dollars ($3,000,000,000); or (ii) has a Credit Rating equal to or better

cites.section: Attachment G, Retail Customer Form ESA, sections 14 and 14.1
cites.quote: than BBB- from S&P or Baa3 from Moody’s

cites.section: Attachment G, Retail Customer Form ESA, section 14.1
cites.quote: Upon the happening and during the continuance of a Credit Event, then within 30 days of demand from Company to Customer, Customer shall provide to Company either (a) a cash deposit, (b) a letter of credit, (c) a surety bond, or (d) other credit support in a form and from an entity reasonably acceptable to Company, in the amount of Company’s credit exposure over the remaining term of this Agreement, which credit exposure shall not exceed the Guaranty Cap.

exit_fee.value: Exit fee on 80 percent of contracted capacity (the Commission raised it from Xcel's 75 percent). In Xcel's proposed sheet: termination on 24 months' notice with an exit fee equal to Effective Contract Capacity x on-peak demand charges x the percentage x the lesser of the remaining ESA months or 120 months; the same formula applies to a contract capacity reduction (12 months' notice in the form ESA)

cites.section: Key approvals, A balanced contract structure
cites.quote: the Commission increased the minimum bill and exit fee proposed by Xcel to 80% of the customer’s contracted capacity to strengthen ratepayer protections.
Upon 24 months’ notice by the Customer, subject to payment of exit fee

Early termination or Contract Capacity reduction shall incur fees calculated as the total of (i) the Effective Contract Capacity multiplied by (ii) the on peak demand charges contained in this rate schedule multiplied by (iii) seventy-five percent (75%) multiplied by (iv) the “Termination Period,” defined as the lesser of the remaining contract months of the ESA Term or 120 months from the date of the Termination Notice as defined in the ESA.

cites.section: Attachment G, Retail Customer Form ESA, section 16.1
cites.quote: no less than twelve (12) months in the case of Capacity Reduction

quoted_clause.quote: The commission may approve, modify, or reject a tariff or electric service agreement proposed between a public utility and a very large customer establishing the terms and conditions under which the utility will provide electric service to the customer.

docket.value: Laws 2025, First Special Session, chapter 12, section 9; amended 2026 c 88 art 1 s 91

cites.quote: Signed by the governor June 14, 2025, 10:30 a.m.
This section is effective the day following final enactment.

threshold_mw.value: No MW figure in the statute: the Commission defines the very large customer class or subclass for each utility by order by 15 December 2026

cites.quote: By December 15, 2026, the commission shall establish by order the definition and appropriate characteristics of a very large customer class or subclass for each public utility providing electric service.

min_demand.searched: Minn. Stat. § 216B.1622 subds. 1 to 3 and Laws 2025, 1Sp c 12 s 9: the statute requires protections against stranded costs but sets no minimum demand or bill

queue_size.value: see row: Large General Time of Day Service (Rate Code AXX, Minnesota Electric Rate Book MPUC No. 2, Section No. 5, Sheets 32.2 to 32.7): the very large customer tariff

rows.license_basis: the State's official publication of its statutes and session laws
rows.notes: Required outcomes the Commission must consider (subd. 2): costs of very large customers assigned to their class; electricity meeting the § 216B.1691 benchmarks; protections so other customers are not placed at risk for stranded costs. Subd. 3: the section does not apply to existing, renewed or extended ESAs or to very large customers taking service before 2020. Related definition (Minn. Stat. § 216B.02, subd. 11, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.02): a data center is a facility designed to have a load of 100 megawatts or more. The MPUC's data center page (https://mn.gov/puc/activities/v-l-e-c/data-centers/) names §§ 216B.1622 and 216B.1623 and an annual ECO fund fee of 2 to 5 million dollars for qualified large-scale data centers (not a connection term). Status date as the reading group wrote it: '2025-06-14 (signed; the section is effective the day following final enactment)'. Corrected by the independent audit of session 5304 (A-29): the status date was '2025-06-14', the governor's signature; the act takes effect 'the day following final enactment', a date the text does not print.

exit_fee.value: Minimum bill payments after termination for the lesser of 15 years or the remaining initial or renewal term (the 15 years counting the 24-month notice period plus 13 years of payments after termination)

Determination of the number of the term period for calculating the Exit Fee includes the required 24-month termination notice period described in the Auto-Renewal term below and thirteen years of Minimum Bill payments following termination.

threshold_mw.value: 20 MW minimum demand at 161 kV; 200 MW at 345 kV (customer-owned substation); demand must reach the minimum within 18 months

cites.quote: The minimum Demand for service under this Rate Schedule is 20,000 kilowatts for service at 161,000 volts or a minimum Demand of 200,000 kilowatts for service at 345,000 volts each month.

Customers must substantiate to OPPD’s satisfaction that their Demand requirements will meet the minimum Demand requirements of this Rate Schedule within 18 months of establishing service under this Rate Schedule.

min_demand.value: Minimum billing demand of 20,000 kW (161 kV) or 200,000 kW (345 kV) a month; minimum monthly bill 488,200 dollars (161 kV) or 4,792,000 dollars (345 kV); billing demand also not below 90 percent of the highest summer demand or 75 percent of the highest non-summer demand of the preceding 11 months

cites.quote: Minimum Billing Demand of 20,000 kilowatts per month for interconnection at 161,000 volts or 200,000 kilowatts per month for interconnection at 345,000 volts.
Minimum Monthly Bill: $488,200 for Customers taking service at 161,000 volts or $4,792,000 for Customers taking service at 345,000 volts

The Customer’s Demand must be equal to or greater than the larger of the following: ... 90% of the highest 15-minute Power Factor-adjusted Demand during the Summer billing months of the preceding eleven (11) months, or ... 75% of the highest 15-minute Power Factor-adjusted Demand during the Non-Summer billing months of the preceding eleven (11) months
